clue.text: Pass round poster shortly with one earning a crust?

indicators.note: round says the Alpine pass name goes around the other pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: the Brenner Pass is an Alpine crossing between Austria and Italy
a poster is an advertisement, an ad

indicators.note: shortly says the word with is cut short, losing its last letters

parts.note: the word with, trimmed

explanation.surface: Someone hands round a short poster to a worker who makes their living.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' and 'round' are the indicators. 'one' looks like I, but the definition needs it: a breadwinner is one who earns a crust.
explanation.definitionFit: Earning a crust is idiom for making a living, and the family member doing that is its main earner.

clue.text: Area of ill repute for ships with rig alerting problem

definitions.text: Area of ill repute for ships

parts.note: a Bermuda rig is a sailing rig; rig also means outfit, and Bermudas are shorts

indicators.note: problem suggests the letters of alerting are in trouble and must be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A stretch of sea notorious for losing vessels, where a ship's rigging keeps sounding the alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'problem' is the anagram signal. A Bermuda rig is a sailing rig, which suits the ships; the blogger read 'rig' as an outfit of Bermuda shorts.
explanation.definitionFit: This stretch of the western Atlantic is legendary for ships and planes that vanished there.

clue.text: Inspiration for poetry and from time to time love

parts.note: an era is a period of time
an era is a period of time
love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: What inspires poetry, and love that comes now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from time to time' reads as 'now and then' but splits into time, to (a link) and time again.
explanation.definitionFit: She is the Muse of lyric and love poetry in Greek myth, so a source of poetic inspiration.

clue.text: Two lines from a parodist I cherish

indicators.note: from says the answer is taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A couplet borrowed from a parodist the speaker loves.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair of verse lines forming a unit is the technical term from prosody for a couplet.

clue.text: Beastly sound, almost senseless outside

indicators.note: outside says the trimmed word for senseless goes around the word for sound
almost says the last letter of the word for senseless is dropped

parts.note: senseless means inane
a hum is a low sound

explanation.surface: An animal noise, nearly meaningless, heard from outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' and 'outside' are the indicators; 'Beastly' sounds like an animal noise in the surface but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Beastly behaviour is cruel and brutish, lacking the qualities of a decent person.

clue.text: Pest is in subtle shade

indicators.note: in places the word is inside the word for a subtle shade

parts.note: a nuance is a subtle shade of meaning or colour
taken as written

explanation.surface: An insect found in a delicate shade of colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A pest is an annoying person or thing, a synonym for an irritation.

clue.text: Ignoring qualms of Yorkshire hooligans on carrier?

parts.note: Yorkshire was historically split into three Ridings, so a riding is a part of Yorkshire
roughs are rowdy hooligans
a hod is a builder's tray for carrying bricks

explanation.surface: Northern thugs ride on a vehicle without a care for anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: The RIDINGS were the old administrative divisions of Yorkshire, a large English county.
explanation.definitionFit: To act this way is to proceed without regard for others' feelings or scruples, an idiom.

clue.text: AA author's grasping heavyweight clue in place of OU

indicators.note: grasping says the author's name holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: A. A. Milne wrote Winnie-the-Pooh; with the possessive this gives Milne's
a ton is a heavy weight
a key is a clue to a puzzle

explanation.surface: Winnie-the-Pooh's creator holds a heavyweight hint about where the Open University lives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grasping' is the container signal. OU is the Open University, the UK's distance-learning university, headquartered in this Buckinghamshire new town.
explanation.definitionFit: The Open University's main campus is in this English new town, so it is where the OU is based.

clue.text: See 7
Entrances made by trespassers?

parts.note: an encroachment read literally as people making routes into land they should not enter

explanation.definitionFit: Making these is to advance into or encroach on territory, read here as trespassers' ways in.

clue.text: It effects change on top — in novelist, that is

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for that is inside the novelist's name

parts.note: Thomas Hardy, the English novelist
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is; its first letter goes inside
the second letter of the abbreviation i.e., placed after the name

explanation.surface: Something altering the look at the top, as found in a novelist's work, that is.
explanation.walkthrough: Only part of IE goes in: the I sits inside HARDY and the E follows it, a loose 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: A colouring product changes the shade of one's hair, the top of the head.

clue.text: I must note effect of putting verbs at end of clauses, say

definitions.text: putting verbs at end of clauses, say

indicators.note: effect of says the letters of these words are worked into a new result

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A grammar note on what happens when verbs go to the end of clauses.
explanation.walkthrough: German sends verbs to the end of subordinate clauses; 'say' marks it as one example of a Germanic trait.
explanation.definitionFit: A German idiom or characteristic, such as verb-final word order, is an example of Germanic style.

clue.text: UN man once on Solway Firth

definitions.meaning: Kofi ... was a former Secretary-General of the United Nations
a Scottish town on the river of the same name near the Solway Firth

explanation.definitionFit: The surname of a former UN Secretary-General is also a town in Dumfriesshire, near the Solway Firth.

clue.text: Trim and plain, like "ox"

definitions.meaning: plain, as a drink served without mixer or ice
an old word for cattle; Chambers gives it as meaning an ox, cow or bull

explanation.definitionFit: The one word means tidy, undiluted (of a spirit), and in old usage cattle such as an ox.

clue.text: Beast of an old number "Following that endless river, Love"

indicators.note: Following says the old number comes after the trimmed river in the answer
endless says the river's name loses its final letter

parts.note: the Rhine is a major European river
OC read as an old way of writing a hundred, C being the Roman numeral for 100
Eros is the Greek god of love

explanation.surface: An animal from an old song about following an endless river to love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' and 'Following' are the indicators. The surface reads like a song title; OC as an old hundred is Araucaria's loose usage.
explanation.definitionFit: This large horned African or Asian mammal is a beast in the plainest sense.

clue.text: See 23
Old bouncer trained to get award as cook

indicators.note: trained says the letters are put through a course and come out reshaped

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A retired doorman retrains and wins a cookery prize.
explanation.definitionFit: This French phrase names a top culinary distinction and, by extension, a first-class cook.

clue.text: An officer on a horse shows his metal

indicators.note: on in a down clue says the following pieces sit below the horse

parts.note: a cob is a sturdy short-legged horse
Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant, an officer

explanation.surface: A mounted officer displays his mettle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shows his metal' plays on 'mettle', courage; the definition is just 'metal'.
explanation.definitionFit: This hard silvery-blue element is a metal used in alloys and blue pigments.

clue.text: American yetis, fewer than three in the yard?

definitions.meaning: North American ape-like creatures of legend, like the yeti

definitions.text: fewer than three in the yard?
definitions.meaning: a yard is three feet; large feet would fit fewer than three into it

explanation.definitionFit: Plural of the legendary North American creature; also simply oversized feet, too large for three to make a yard.

clue.text: Established in place at last, taking the mickey somewhat

parts.note: the end is what comes at last

indicators.note: somewhat says only part of the words the mickey is used

explanation.surface: Settled at last and teasing someone a little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' is a link; 'somewhat' takes EMIC from 'thE MICkey'.
explanation.definitionFit: A disease or species native to and regularly found in one region is described this way.

clue.text: Light in bed?

definitions.meaning: something planted in a flower bed, such as a tulip root

explanation.definitionFit: It is both the glass part of an electric light and the root of a plant set in a garden bed.

clue.text: Year after car inventor left type of alcohol

indicators.note: after says the abbreviation for year follows the inventor's name

parts.note: Karl Benz built the first practical motor car

explanation.surface: A year after the motor car's inventor departed, some kind of drink appeared.
explanation.definitionFit: Benzyl alcohol is an aromatic alcohol used as a solvent, so the word names an alcohol type.

clue.text: Well done, thug!

definitions.meaning: a cry of applause meaning well done
a hired ruffian or assassin, especially in Italian usage

explanation.definitionFit: It is both a shout of praise and, in Chambers, a hired desperado or bandit.

clue.text: Old Tory statesman on leave with swimmer

parts.note: to go is to leave
a dolphin is a swimming sea mammal

explanation.surface: An elderly Conservative politician goes on holiday to swim with a marine mammal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on leave' reads as holiday; 'on' is a link and 'leave' gives GO.
explanation.definitionFit: Sidney Godolphin was Lord Treasurer under Queen Anne, a statesman associated with the Tories.

clue.text: Old countrywoman to see about parking eggs (she married 8)

parts.note: Lydia was an ancient country in Asia Minor, and also a woman's name

indicators.note: about says the word for see goes round the abbreviation for parking

parts.note: to look is to see
ova are eggs

explanation.surface: An old rural woman sees about parking her eggs before her wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts P inside LOOK. The Russian ballerina wed the economist John Maynard Keynes in 1925.
explanation.definitionFit: This Russian ballet dancer was the wife of the economist Keynes, whose surname is 8's answer.

clue.text: Student expressions of disgust and approval at access to organ

parts.note: L, the learner plate, stands for a student
ugh expresses disgust
ole is a cheer of approval

explanation.surface: A student groans in disgust and cheers approval on reaching a church organ.
explanation.walkthrough: A LUGHOLE is British slang for the ear; 'organ' is the ear, not the instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for the ear, the opening into the organ of hearing.

clue.text: Cut long grass in the sun?

definitions.text: Cut long grass in the sun?

parts.words: Cut long grass in the sun?
parts.note: mowing and drying grass while the weather is fine, as the proverb advises

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means took advantage of an opportunity, from the proverb about the sun shining.

clue.text: Flexible musicians are a tie

parts.note: elastic means flexible or stretchy
a band is a group of musicians

explanation.surface: Adaptable musicians end up level with their rivals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a tie' looks like a drawn match; here it is something that ties things together.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubber loop used to bind items together serves as a simple tie.
